risks: Minimal: recording care already given and an existing follow-up call.
consent: Exempt as quality assurance with publication permitted (REB-EX-26-311); patients are informed through the pre-operative leaflet and may decline the use of their data for publication.
data: Forms hold a study number; linkage to surveillance is by the infection prevention team; reports never identify individual surgeons or theatre staff.
equity: PROGRESS-Plus: older patients, people living alone, people with limited English and people without a phone are most likely to be missed by the day-30 call, and emergency patients receive fewer elements. Interpreters are used for calls, a clinic check replaces unanswered calls, and results are reported for emergency and elective cases and by age.
effectiveness: Shows where the bundle fails and whether full delivery goes with fewer infections.
efficiency: Existing surveillance plus two minutes per operation.
partnerships: Infection prevention, theatre nursing, anaesthesia, two patient partners who had wound infections, and the regional surgical quality network.
rebPath: REB exemption as quality assurance with publication permitted (REB-EX-26-311); ICH-GCP and Declaration of Helsinki principles for confidentiality.
limitations: Observational; residual confounding; recording may change practice.
summary: Minimal-risk study under an REB exemption with attention to patients hard to reach after discharge.
